facts.statement: Eudimorphodon was discovered in 1973 by Mario Pandolfi in Cene, Italy, and described by Rocco Zambelli the same year.
facts.quote: Eudimorphodon is an extinct genus of pterosaur that was discovered in 1973 by Mario Pandolfi in the town of Cene, Italy and described the same year by Rocco Zambelli.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon lived during the Late Triassic (219–215 million years ago) and is one of the oldest known pterosaurs.
facts.quote: The nearly complete skeleton was retrieved from shale deposited during the Late Triassic (mid to late Norian stage, 219-215 million years ago), making Eudimorphodon one of the oldest pterosaurs known.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon had a wingspan of about 100 cm.
facts.quote: It had a wingspan of about 100 cm.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon was a small pterosaur, about 1 meter long and weighing no more than 10 kg.
facts.quote: Eudimorphodon was a small pterosaur, being 1 m in length, and weighing no more than 10 kg.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon had a very large fourth finger that supported the wing membrane.
facts.quote: Its fourth finger had a very large size, and attached to the membrane making up the wing.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon had fangs (four upper, two lower per side) followed by smaller multi-cusped teeth (25 upper, 26 lower, mostly with five cusps).
facts.quote: The front of the jaw was filled with fangs, per side four in the upper jaw, two in the lower jaw, that rather abruptly gave way to a line of smaller multipointed teeth, 25 in the upper jaw, 26 in the lower jaw, most of which had five cusps

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon was piscivorous, confirmed by preserved stomach contents containing fish of the genus Parapholidophorus.
facts.quote: The morphology of the teeth are suggestive of a piscivorous diet, which has been confirmed by preserved stomach contents containing the remains of fish of the genus Parapholidophorus.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon had the strongest dental occlusion known among pterosaurs, with top and bottom teeth touching directly when jaws closed.
facts.quote: The top and bottom teeth of Eudimorphodon came into direct contact with each other when the jaws were closed, especially at the back of the jaw. This degree of dental occlusion is the strongest known among pterosaurs.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon could crush or chew its food, as shown by multi-cusped teeth and tooth wear.
facts.quote: The teeth were multi-cusped, and tooth wear shows that Eudimorphodon was able to crush or chew its food to some degree.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon likely fed on hard-shelled invertebrates, indicated by wear along the sides of its teeth.
facts.quote: Wear along the sides of these teeth suggests that Eudimorphodon also fed on hard-shelled invertebrates.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon's multi-cusped teeth distinguish it from almost all other pterosaurs, which had simple teeth or none.
facts.quote: The teeth distinguish Eudimorphodon, because almost all other pterosaurs either had simple teeth, or lacked them altogether.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon may have had a diamond-shaped structure at the end of its long bony tail, similar to later Rhamphorhynchus.
facts.quote: en el final de su larga cola ósea puede haber tenido una estructura en forma de diamante como en el más tardío Rhamphorhynchus.

facts.statement: If present, the diamond-shaped tail structure may have acted as a rudder to help steer Eudimorphodon in the air.
facts.quote: Si era el caso, este diamante puede haber servido como un timón que ayudaba a dirigirlo mientras maniobraba en el aire.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon is believed to be a member of the specialized off-branch Campylognathoididae.
facts.quote: Instead it is believed to be a member of a specialized off branch from the main "line" of pterosaur evolution, the Campylognathoididae.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Matthew G. Baron suggests Eudimorphodon groups with the clade Novialoidea within Lonchognatha, differing from the Campylognathoididae placement.
facts.quote: In 2020 however, a study upheld by Matthew G. Baron about early pterosaur interrelationships found Eudimorphodon to group with the clade Novialoidea, both within the clade called Lonchognatha.

facts.statement: Fossil jaw fragments with multi-cusped teeth were found in 1986 in the Dockum Group rocks of western Texas.
facts.quote: In 1986 fossil jaw fragments containing multicusped teeth were found in Dockum Group rocks in western Texas.

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon is classified within the subfamily Eudimorphodontinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Eudimorphodontinae

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon includes the species E. ranzii (1973) and E. cromptonellus (2001).
facts.quote: subdivision: E. ranzii Zambelli, 1973 E. cromptonellus Jenkins , 2001

facts.statement: Eudimorphodon possessed few primitive characteristics, making it of little use for determining where pterosaurs fit in the reptile family tree.
facts.quote: Eudimorphodon tenía pocas características primitivas haciendo a este taxón de poco uso en tratar de averiguar dónde encajan los pterosaurios en el árbol de familia de los reptiles.

facts.statement: It retained basal traits such as pterygoid teeth and a flexible tail lacking the rigid vertebral extensions found in other long-tailed pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Sin embargo tiene rasgos basales, como la retención de dientes pterigoides y la flexibilidad de la cola, la que carece de las rígidas extensiones vertebrales que otros pterosaurios de cola larga poseían.

facts.statement: Due to a scarcity of primitive pterosaur remains, its evolutionary origins remain a mystery, with some experts suggesting affinities with dinosauriforms, arcosauriforms, or prolacertiforms.
facts.quote: La escasez de restos de pterosaurios primitivos ha asegurado hasta ahora que sus orígenes evolutivos contunúen siendo un persistente misterio con algunos expertos que sugieren afinidades con los dinosauriformes, los arcosauriformes o los prolacertiformes.

facts.statement: It is believed to be a member of a specialized branch of pterosaur evolution, the family Campylognathoididae, separate from the main lineage.
facts.quote: En vez de ello se cree que es un miembro de una rama especializada apartada de la "línea" principal de la evolución de los pterosaurios, la familia Campylognathoididae.

facts.statement: Its multicuspided teeth are considered a highly derived trait compared to the single-cusped teeth of Jurassic pterosaurs.
facts.quote: sus dientes multicúspides se consideran como un rasgo altamente derivado, comparados a los dientes de una sola cúspide de los pterosaurios del Jurásico

facts.statement: The type species, E. ranzii, was described by Zambelli in 1973.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, E. ranzii, fue descrita por Zambelli en 1973.

facts.statement: The species name honors Professor Silvio Ranzi.
facts.quote: El nombre científico de la especie honra al profesor Silvio Ranzi.

facts.statement: A second species, E. rosenfeldi, was named by Dalla Vecchia in 1995 based on two specimens found in Italy.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, E. rosenfeldi, fue nombrada por Dalla Vecchia en 1995 a partir de dos especímens hallados en Italia.

facts.statement: However, further studies by Dalla Vecchia found these specimens represented a distinct genus, which he named Carniadactylus in 2009.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estudios adicionales hechos por Dalla Vecchia hallaron que estos realmente representaban un género distinto, el cual él denominó Carniadactylus en 2009.

facts.statement: An additional species, E. cromptonellus, was described by Jenkins and colleagues in 2001.
facts.quote: E. cromptonellus, descrita por Jenkins y colegas en 2001.

facts.statement: The species name is a diminutive tribute to Professor Alfred W. Crompton due to the small size of the specimen.
facts.quote: Su nombre de especie es un homenaje al profesor Alfred W. Crompton; el nombre es un diminutivo debido a lo pequeño del ejemplar.

facts.statement: In 1986, fragments of jaws containing multicuspided teeth were found in rocks of the Dockum Group in west Texas.
facts.quote: En 1986 fragmentos de mandíbulas que contenían dientes multicúspides fueron hallados en las rocas del Grupo Dockum en el oeste de Texas.

facts.statement: One fragment, apparently from a lower jaw, contained two teeth, each with five cusps.
facts.quote: Un fragmento, aparentemente de una mandíbula inferior, contenía dos dientes, cada uno de cinco puntas.

facts.statement: Another fragment from an upper jaw also contained several multicuspided teeth.
facts.quote: Otro fragmento, de una mandíbula superior, también contenía varios dientes multicúspides.

facts.statement: These findings are very similar to Eudimorphodon and could be attributable to that genus, though it is impossible to be certain without better fossil remains.
facts.quote: Estos hallazgos son muy similares a Eudimorphodon y podrían ser atribuibles a ese género, aunque sin mejores restos fósiles es imposible estar seguro.

facts.statement: It was featured in an episode of Animal Planet's Animal Armageddon, described as a gull-like creature feeding on fish and carrion.
facts.quote: Eudimorphodon fue representado en un episodio de la serie de Animal Planet Animal Armageddon, donde fue descrito como una criatura similar a una gaviota, alimentándose de peces y carroña.

facts.statement: Its parent group is Campylognathoididae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Campylognathoididae

facts.statement: Its family is Campylognathoididae.
facts.quote: Family: Campylognathoididae

facts.statement: It belongs to the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: It lived from the Norian to the Rhaetian stages, between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (227.3 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 13 recorded fossil occurrences of this genus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 13
